temporal.retrospective_vs_point_in_time_note: Two distinct questions, never conflated: RETROSPECTIVE analysis ('what actually happened historically?') can query every accepted canonical event regardless of when it was ingested. POINT-IN-TIME intelligence ('what was knowable as of a particular moment?') uses events_as_of()'s strict ingestion_time <= as_of filter (app/intelligence/temporal.py, UNCHANGED) and will, correctly, exclude backfilled history from any as_of before it was actually ingested -- see docs/CALIBRATION_METHODOLOGY.md's own 'bulk backfill' finding (Milestone 2), reconfirmed, not re-litigated, here. This harness never weakens that filter to make a backfilled dataset look more complete.

notes: 13 site(s) have a label that cannot yet be confirmed (the 30-day prediction horizon has not fully elapsed as of real "now") -- reported as UNAVAILABLE, never coerced into a negative label.

observation_incident_temporal.methodology_note: Descriptive co-occurrence only. Each bucket below reports how many OBSERVATION events and how many incident-sheet events (any raw Incident Type) fell in the same site/time window, computed from the exact same events_as_of() query builder (app/intelligence/temporal.py, UNCHANGED) every other trend calculation in this codebase uses. This is NOT a correlation coefficient, NOT a statistical test, and NOT a causal claim -- a project with observations and incidents in the same period is not thereby shown to have one cause the other. See the task's own explicit instruction: 'same-project observation + incident = causal relationship' must not be assumed. Deliberately RETROSPECTIVE, not point-in-time: it queries every accepted canonical event by event_time alone (events_as_of(..., strict_point_in_time=False)), not gated by ingestion_time -- the 'what did this dataset's own history actually contain' question TemporalIntegrityReport's own retrospective-vs-point-in-time note already distinguishes from a live feature computation. A strict point-in-time reading (ingestion_time <= as_of) of a real dataset that was bulk-ingested just now would, correctly, show ~zero events in every bucket except the most recent -- the same 'bulk backfill collapses into the most recent bucket' behavior already documented from Milestone 2, reconfirmed against this real dataset, not a bug in this analysis. Using it here would answer a different question than the one item 11 asks.

supported_conclusions: Observation reporting volume (all categories, and specifically unsafe-observation reporting) increased over the analysis window, triggering the existing UNSAFE_OBSERVATION_SURGE signal.
Most projects with substantial observation volume in the analysis window recorded zero incidents (e.g. ATLANTIS PERIWINKLE: 184 observations / 0 incidents).
Every provenance chain checked (1045/1045) is intact end to end.

The dataset's second Status column is empirically a data-quality/review flag (Closed<->REVIEW REQUIRED 959/959, Open<->OK 41/41), not a restatement of the business open/closed lifecycle -- confirmed independently by the reconciliation workbook.
unsupported_conclusions_explicitly_not_c: That increased observation volume reflects a change in underlying site safety.
That any project with zero recorded incidents is thereby shown to be safe.
That same-project observation and incident co-occurrence is a causal relationship.
Any predictive accuracy, PR-AUC, ROC-AUC, precision, recall, or calibration performance -- no model was trained.
architecture_limitations_discovered: A live as_of=now evaluation of bulk-backfilled historical data cannot produce a single confirmed predictive label for any site, because the prediction horizon is inherently unelapsed relative to real now.

bucketed_counts() does not expose events_as_of()'s own strict_point_in_time parameter, so the observation-vs-incident temporal analysis (item 11) had to reimplement its bucketing loop locally to run it in retrospective mode.
The existing terminology alias table (built from synthetic scenarios) resolves only 49% of this dataset's Incident Type vocabulary and 57% of its Category vocabulary.
The Real Enterprise Dataset Evaluation Specification referenced by this task was not supplied to this session.
recommendations_for_next_milestone: Human-reviewed terminology alias additions for NearMiss, PropertyDamage, FireIncident, VehicleAccident, SecurityBreach, and the 11 unmapped Category terms -- proposed, not applied.
Re-run predictive readiness with an explicit historical as_of (30+ days before the dataset's own latest date) to get a genuine positive/negative label reading.
Obtain and evaluate against the Real Enterprise Dataset Evaluation Specification, if one exists.
Extend bucketed_counts() with an optional strict_point_in_time passthrough.

Do not proceed to advanced ML, autonomous agents, automated interventions/retraining, external web intelligence, production deployment, or new intelligence algorithms without a separate, explicit approval.
